title: SHOW-E-MOTIONS
subtitle: A Wearable Interface for Radical Emotional Visibility
summary: A heart-rate-driven garment that turns private physiological change into a public, moving image.
statement: If emotion becomes visible, does the body gain agency—or become newly exposed?
body: Show-E-Motions is a collaborative inquiry into affective technology, fashion and moving image. Heart-rate data is translated into real-time projection mapping on a textile body, transforming an internal signal into a shared visual event. The garment stops behaving as a covering and becomes an interface: expressive, unstable and impossible to ignore.

sections.body: Three moving-image studies explore restrained, withdrawn and surging visual intensities. These are expressive interpretations of physiological change, rather than measurements of a specific emotion.

sections.title: Affective Ecology
sections.body: Before designing a sensor, the team looked at how living organisms make internal condition visible through colour, scale and posture. Show-E-Motions asks what changes when a human body borrows this legibility inside a social world trained to suppress anxiety.
sections.caption: 03 / RESEARCH

blocks.title: What if clothing could signal from within?
blocks.body: Animal colour and shape became prompts for speculative fashion: could a future garment make internal change perceptible without fixing its meaning? Show-E-Motions does not claim that heart rate reveals a person’s true emotion. A pulse remains ambiguous—exertion, fear, joy and anticipation can overlap—and the project treats that ambiguity as material rather than reducing the body to a clean label.
blocks.caption: RESEARCH / BIOLOGICAL SIGNALS AND CRITICAL POSITION

sections.title: From Pulse to Projection
sections.body: From that research question, the project builds a translation chain rather than a single object. A physical signal is sensed, interpreted, converted into image behaviour and returned to the body as light.

sections.title: Making Radical Honesty
sections.body: The interface only exists because code, cloth and the body are negotiated together. Dyeing, memory fabric, sculptural patterning, mannequin tests and live projection turn the proposition into a wearable encounter.

blocks.title: Radical honesty—or radical exposure?
blocks.body: Making hidden signals visible can challenge emotional suppression and give form to experiences that are difficult to articulate. It can also create pressure to disclose, perform or be interpreted by others. Show-E-Motions holds both possibilities at once: the body gains a new language, but not a final translation.
blocks.caption: IF EMOTION BECOMES VISIBLE, WHO CONTROLS ITS MEANING?
